scope: Two deliberately idle Tailscale-down faults on the existing private Linux host, observed through authenticated owner and distinct recipient Chrome sessions. The recipient held one new, one-hour, three-file read-only grant. No active task, model call, or new release was involved.

recipient_check.identity: Previously verified second Google OIDC identity in a separate Chrome incognito profile; identifiers omitted

limits: The recipient check exercised an inspect-only session with no active Kata job submitted through the browser. It does not combine authenticated browser entry and active-job termination in one fault.
Chrome's network error was observed after the fault, but no browser request timing or hard outage deadline was measured.

The owner browser showed a sign-in page after its fault and a fresh Google OIDC sign-in succeeded. A distinct recipient session remained authenticated after the later fault, so the cause of the owner's sign-in state was not isolated.
The close hook could not verify the normal inbound shield after tailnet down and used its daemon-blocking fallback. This observed fallback does not prove a universal deadline or recovery reliability.
The separate fifth root-only active-Kata fault passed its bounded checks; neither browser check is the same end-to-end active-job test.
Historical failed active-fault attempts and the unexplained fourth-attempt relapse remain open. Broad security assurance and pilot readiness remain unproven.
